m2-face-a.title: Face A - stale DIGEST at the seam, asserted in code
m2-face-a.imperative: Drive the scratch spine so a why_trail record names an early PRE-TRIP understanding, then move to a later gate and get part-way through it so the agent's real understanding has moved on. Trip HARD, run the literal 'attach <gate> --type refresh-request --field seam=... --field why_ref=...' the refusal prints, then STOP without advancing. Assert in code that the DIGEST: line a cold successor reads from `current` STILL names the pre-trip understanding. Assert as equality/in against the pre-trip text, not by eyeballing. The RED is end-to-end staleness, not 'advance raises'.

why_trail.why: Handoff is complete and its central trap is understood: the shipped HARD refusal RELEASES once a keyed refresh-request exists, so an exception-only repro proves nothing. The real defect is that advance is the sole why_trail writer, so a refused advance leaves _latest_why_record pointing at the PREVIOUS gate's understanding, and _why_suffix therefore prints a DIGEST that is stale by exactly one gate to a cold successor. Repro must assert that equality in code and must show the CONTEXT (>= hard) advisory to prove the planted gauge was read.

Harness green at exit 0. The scratch spine is built by real engine verbs only (claim/start/attest/advance) and the gauge is planted as a SIBLING of that scratch spine, never the live one. The being-read proof is a silence/advisory pair on the SAME spine and session: no CONTEXT line before the gauge exists, then the engine's own 'CONTEXT 30% (>= hard)' line after -- so a later 'nothing happened' can never be confused with a silent governor. Discovered:  takes no --session-id, which is also the more faithful cold-successor read.

Face A reproduced at exit 0, end to end, as staleness rather than as an exception. After the agent runs the literal attach the refusal prints, the HARD band RELEASES -- the engine switches to 'refresh already requested for g2, hand off now' -- yet the same output still reads DIGEST: PRE-TRIP UNDERSTANDING. Asserted as an equality against the pre-trip text, and the current understanding is asserted absent from both the output and the trail. A counterfactual run of the identical spine with no gauge advances the same gate and yields the fresh DIGEST, so the staleness is attributable to the refusal and nothing else.

Face B reproduced at exit 0. At HARD the advance refusal names only the context limit; with the gauge rewritten below hard the same advance refuses with 'postconditions unmet [c2]'. Both refusal texts captured, asserted different, and the hard one asserted not to name c2. Honest scope added and asserted: current DOES still list c2 [unmet] at HARD, so the masking is scoped to the advance refusal path -- an agent that acts on the refusal text hands off believing context was its only blocker.

Closeout verified. Single command 'python .agent-work/issue-467-trip-semantics/red-repro/repro_431.py --all' wipes the whole scratch root and reproduces both faces: 24 ASSERT OK, 0 ASSERT FAIL, real exit 0. Source diff for scripts and tests is zero bytes, checked twice via redirect with the exit read separately. Suite at baseline: 1793 passed, 2 skipped, 683 subtests, real exit 0. Result written to crew-handoffs/g1-implementer-result.md, including one empirically verified triage candidate: copy-pasting the refusal's literal why_ref placeholder attaches successfully but does not release HARD.
